items.headline: Restricted KA vs Mechanical Alignment: Function Up, Fear Unchanged

blocks.metric: Longitudinal outcome, rKA vs MA (mixed model)

blocks.text: Falling kinesiophobia tracked with better OKS/FJS in both groups, whichever alignment was used.

items.message: rKA gives a modest functional edge, but kinesiophobia needs its own psychological and rehab targeting.
items.title: Restricted Kinematic Alignment Improves Function, But Does Not Reduce Kinesiophobia After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A 3-Year Follow-Up Study.

items.headline: Tibial Tubercle Osteotomy for Patellar Instability
items.message: Bony complications are rare; counsel patients mainly about painful hardware, stiffness and failure-related reoperation.
items.title: Tibial Tuberosity Osteotomy for Patellar Instability Has Low Complication Rates and Favorable Patient-Reported Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

items.headline: Quadriceps Autograft: All-Soft-Tissue vs Bone Block

blocks.text: No study found a difference in failure or return to sport. Both intraoperative patellar fractures occurred in the bone-block group.

items.message: Short-term outcomes look equivalent; the bone block carries a small, specific patellar fracture risk.
items.title: Quadriceps Tendon Autograft for Primary Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Has No Difference in Short-Term Clinical Outcomes Between All-Soft Tissue Versus Tendon-Bone Grafts: A Systematic Review.

items.headline: Adding Centralization to MMPRT Repair

blocks.text: The one RCT still saw extrusion rise after centralization, though less than with isolated root repair.

items.message: Root repair plus centralization improves PROMs and controls extrusion in the short term, with few complications.
items.title: Meniscal Centralization Improves Outcomes and Limits Extrusion After Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Repair: A Systematic Review.

items.headline: Where Open-Wedge HTO Goes Off-Plan

rows: Less slope gain, more internal rotation

blocks.text: Each 1° of internal rotation cost 1.6 points on the 1-year Lysholm score.

items.message: Watch anteromedial gap opening and axial rotation, not just the coronal angle.
items.title: Anteromedial Gap Opening and Osteotomy Sufficiency Are Associated With Multiplanar Correction Errors in Open-Wedge High Tibial Osteotomy: A Computed Tomography-Based Study.

items.headline: Aseptic Revision TKA: Who Re-Fails?

blocks.text: Instability failures were front-loaded: 7 of 9 occurred within 3.2 years.

items.message: Use the least constraint necessary and watch instability revisions closely in the early years.
items.title: Risk Factors for Re-Revision After Aseptic Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: Knees Revised for Instability Re-Fail Early in a Single-Center Cohort With a Mean 14-Year Follow-Up.

items.headline: Hybrid Graft (Semitendinosus + Tape) in MPFL Reconstruction

blocks.label: Kujala score
blocks.foot: 12 months and final follow-up: no significant difference

blocks.text: Patellar tilt and patella–trochlear groove distance did not differ at any time point.

items.message: Adding tape speeds early recovery after MPFL reconstruction; by one year both grafts end up in the same place.
items.title: Short-term benefits of hybrid graft in medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction for recurrent patellar dislocation: A prospective randomized controlled trial with minimum 2-year follow-up.

items.headline: Double-Level Osteotomy vs HTO for Varus Knees
items.message: DLO keeps the joint line flatter with fewer hinge fractures, but at 3 years patients do not feel the difference.
items.why: Hot debate on joint-line obliquity; first pooled DLO vs HTO comparison.
items.title: Double-level osteotomy versus high tibial osteotomy for varus malalignment of the knee: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

items.headline: All-Inside 4-Strand Semitendinosus ACLR at 10+ Years

blocks.text: Higher preoperative Tegner raised failure risk (P = .016). Graft diameter ≤8 vs >8 mm made no difference (17.5% vs 23.9%, P = .44).

items.message: Patients report good outcomes, but 1 in 5 grafts fails over a decade and residual laxity is common.
items.why: A 20.5% 10-year failure rate challenges the all-inside semitendinosus technique.
items.title: Long-Term Failure Rate of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using All-Inside 4-Stranded Semitendinosus Autograft Is 20.5.

items.headline: Standardized PRP Pathway for KL I–II Knee OA
items.message: How PRP is delivered matters: leukocyte-poor PRP, US guidance and staged rehab beat physician-directed PRP.
items.why: A large double-blind multicentre RCT; shows how PRP is delivered changes the result.
items.title: Clinical Pathway Management for Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy in Kellgren-Lawrence Grade I and II Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective, Multicenter, Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.

items.headline: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Before TKA and Thrombotic Events

blocks.label: Risk ratio with preoperative GLP-1 RA

items.message: GLP-1 RA use is associated with fewer MI, DVT and VTE events after TKA; the design is observational and cannot show cause.
items.why: GLP-1 drugs are spreading fast; 23,000 matched TKA patients.
items.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated with Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.

items.headline: Centralization Protects Cartilage After Root Repair (Rabbit Model)

blocks.text: Root repair alone lost central and posterior femoral cartilage on 9.4 T MRI. Extrusion did not differ between groups.

items.message: Animal data support a chondroprotective, zone-specific effect of centralization beyond extrusion control.
items.title: Concomitant Centralization Procedure With Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Repair May Have Zone-Specific Effects on the Medial Femoral Condyle and Enhance Repair Healing Compared With Isolated Root Repair: An In Vivo Experimental Study in Rabbit Knees.

items.headline: Loss of Motion After ACLR in Female Patients

blocks.l: females with BPTB + lateral meniscus repair vs 12% without (P = .004)

items.message: In women, BPTB autograft plus lateral meniscus repair is a high-risk combination for stiffness.
items.title: The use of patellar tendon autograft and lateral meniscus repair are associated with loss of motion of the knee among female patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.

items.headline: Medial Meniscus Repair During Revision ACLR at 10 Years

blocks.text: After adjustment, technique was not an independent predictor (HR 1.62, P = .099).

items.message: Over 80% of medial meniscus repairs done with revision ACLR survive a decade.
items.title: Long-term survivorship of medial meniscus posterior horn repair during revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: 10-year results from the SANTI Group.

items.headline: ACLR in Professional Soccer Players
items.message: Grafts hold up well in elite soccer; the other knee is now the bigger risk.
items.title: Low graft failure after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in professional soccer players: A retrospective cohort study of 232 knees from the SANTI Study Group.

items.headline: Sex Differences After ACLR: 6 Months vs 5 Years

blocks.text: Return-to-sport rates were similar (61% vs 60%). Men showed better quadriceps symmetry at 6 months. Male sex stayed independent after adjustment (OR 1.93).

items.message: Women return to sport just as often but at a lower level, and early strength deficits explain only part of the gap.
items.title: Sex-related differences after ACL reconstruction differ between early functional recovery and 5-year outcomes.

items.headline: NMES After ACL Reconstruction

blocks.label: Isometric quadriceps strength vs standard rehab

blocks.text: NMES also improved flexion, thigh girth and Lysholm, but not IKDC. Isokinetic strength did not differ.

items.message: NMES speeds early strength gains; there is no evidence yet of a long-term functional benefit.
items.title: Neuromuscular Electric Stimulation Improves Early Isometric Knee Strength After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction and Repair: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

items.headline: High-Grade MCL Pie-Crusting During MMPRT Repair
items.message: Aggressive pie-crusting for root repair access did not leave clinically meaningful valgus laxity.
items.title: High-Grade Percutaneous Medial Collateral Ligament Pie-Crusting Is Not Associated With Clinically Meaningful Valgus Instability.

items.headline: Early Limb Symmetry Predicts 2-Year PROMs After QT-ACLR

blocks.text: Isometric quadriceps LSI at 3 months explained 36% of the variance in 2-year IKDC.

items.message: Quadriceps strength at 3 months is an early, actionable predictor of how patients will feel at 2 years.
items.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.

items.headline: TKA After HTO vs TKA After UKA
items.message: Survivorship after conversion is the same; HTO is a sound joint-preserving first step.
items.title: There Were No Differences in Total Knee Arthroplasty Function Following High Tibial Osteotomy or Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: More Than 10 Years of Follow-Up.

items.headline: Bi-Unicompartmental vs CR Total Knee Arthroplasty

blocks.text: 95% CI −17.9 to 8.1 (P = .45). WOMAC, KSS, OKS and VAS were also similar, with no reoperations in either arm.

items.message: Closer to native does not mean clinically better at 2 years in bicompartmental OA.
items.title: Closer to Native, Not Clinically Superior: Bi-Unicompartmental versus Total Knee Arthroplasty for Bicompartmental Femoro-Tibial Osteoarthritis, A Randomized Trial.

items.headline: MCID and PASS After ACLR Are Not One-Size-Fits-All
items.message: Borrowed thresholds may misclassify patients; calculate cohort-specific MCID and PASS values.
items.title: Minimal Clinically Important Difference and Patient Acceptable Symptom State Thresholds After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Vary Considerably Across Published Studies: A Systematic Review.

items.headline: Orthobiologics in ACL Reconstruction

blocks.text: Graft maturation on imaging was unchanged in 6 of 9 trials.

items.message: PRP, BMAC and MSCs add cost without measurable benefit to ACLR outcomes so far.
items.why: Pools RCTs only, and the answer is consistently negative for biologics.
items.title: Orthobiologic Augmentation for Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Is Not Associated With Improved Clinical or Radiographic Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

items.headline: Highly Crosslinked vs Conventional PE in Uncemented TKA

blocks.text: Tibial and femoral component migration (MTPM about 1 mm) and PROMs did not differ at 10 years.

items.message: HXLPE wear plateaus after 5 years while conventional PE wear keeps climbing.
items.why: Rare 10-year blinded RSA trial answering the HXLPE durability question.
items.title: Ten-year insert wear and the migration of uncemented tibial and femoral components with either conventional polyethylene or sequentially annealed highly crosslinked polyethylene: a blinded randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis.

items.headline: Changing CPAK Phenotype in Robotic TKA

blocks.text: A 2-phenotype shift (n = 19) meant smaller OKS gains at 3 and 6 months. LDFA changed by more than 4° gave the smallest gains of all.

items.message: Avoid large departures from the native femoral joint line; femoral changes matter more than tibial ones.
items.title: The impact of changing Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification on early functional outcomes after primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.

items.headline: Revision Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Through 2060
items.message: Growth is driven by the US and China; mature European systems plateau and Japan declines.
items.why: Global 17-country workload forecast; Japan is the outlier that declines.
items.title: Global Projection of Revision Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Through 2060: A 17-Country Analysis Using Worldwide Registry Data.

items.headline: Autograft vs Allograft MPFL Reconstruction in Adolescents

blocks.text: Postoperative Kujala was 84–100 with autograft and 92.7–96.5 with allograft. Autografts had fewer complications.

items.message: Both grafts work in adolescents; autograft may carry fewer complications.
items.title: Autograft Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Reconstruction Provides Comparable Patient-Reported Outcomes and Failure Rates With Fewer Complications Versus Allograft Reconstruction in Adolescent Patients: A Systematic Review.

items.headline: Bridge-Enhanced ACL Restoration (BEAR) After Commercial Release
items.message: Retear rates after BEAR stay low outside trials, and the refined technique cut reoperations sharply.
items.why: First real-world (post-trial) BEAR data outside the original trials.
items.title: Two-year follow-up of postcommercialisation cohort of 100 bridge-enhanced anterior cruciate ligament restorations shows low retear rate and good patient-reported outcomes.

items.headline: All-Inside vs Transtibial Pullout Root Repair
items.message: Both repairs improve function; neither reliably corrects extrusion.
items.title: All-Inside Medial Meniscus Root Repair Improves Function With Results Comparable to Tibial Pullout Method, but Both Methods Fail to Correct Extrusion: A Systematic Review of Clinical and Biomechanical Studies.

items.headline: Unrestricted Kinematic vs Mechanical Alignment TKA

blocks.text: FJS was 91.7 with KA and 82.7 with MA. Stairs, swelling and stiffness did not differ.

items.message: KA may reduce the 'unhappy knee', but this is retrospective, 1-year data.
items.title: Improved function and patient satisfaction with fewer residual symptoms following kinematically versus mechanically aligned total knee arthroplasty: A retrospective study from FP-UCBM Knee Study Group.

items.headline: SIFK Predicts Worse Outcomes After Medial Root Repair

blocks.label: After medial root repair, no SIFK vs SIFK

blocks.text: 37.4% of patients had SIFK on preoperative MRI, and 85% of those were grade 1 or 2.

items.message: Check the preoperative MRI for SIFK before medial root repair, and counsel those patients about less improvement and more reoperation.
items.why: SIFK was present in 37.4% of repairs, even when mostly low grade, and it changes the expected result.
items.title: Preoperative Subchondral Insufficiency Fractures Are Associated With Decreased Clinically Significant Outcome Achievement, Higher Reoperation Rates, and Greater Osteoarthritis Progression After Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Repair at a Minimum 2-Year Follow-Up.

items.headline: Undiagnosed Dysglycemia Is Common Before Orthopaedic Surgery

items.l: best-case floor if all untested patients were normoglycemic
knee arthroscopy, little change with HbA1c

blocks.text: Any complication: adjusted OR 1.1 (1.0–1.2) for undiagnosed diabetes, rising to 2.0 at the worst HbA1c stratum of diagnosed diabetes. Mixed orthopaedic cohort, mainly joint replacement, fracture fixation and spine.

items.message: Undiagnosed dysglycemia did not raise readmission or reoperation, so selective HbA1c testing makes most sense where complications climb, such as hinged and revision TKA.
items.title: Is Undiagnosed Dysglycemia Common in Orthopaedic Surgery and Is it Associated With 30-day Outcomes? A Large-database Study.

items.headline: One Injection of Adipose SVF Beats Placebo in Moderate-to-Severe Knee OA

blocks.metric: Responder rate at 12 months (prespecified composite of pain and function)

blocks.text: Eligibility: WOMAC pain ≥8, Outerbridge 2–4 on MRI, KL 2–4. SVF was isolated at the point of care and injected in the same visit. 618 screened, 114 randomized.

items.message: A same-day autologous SVF injection roughly doubled the responder rate over placebo at 1 year, but the lower CI bound was close to zero and the trial was small.
items.why: First multicentre placebo-controlled trial of point-of-care SVF for knee OA with a positive primary endpoint.
items.title: A Single Intra-articular Injection of Autologous Stromal Vascular Fraction for Moderate-to-Severe Knee Osteoarthritis: Results of a Multicenter Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial With 12-Month Follow-up.

items.headline: Extended Oral TXA After TKA Does Not Reduce Pain or Improve Motion

blocks.label: VAS pain, placebo vs extended oral TXA
blocks.foot: No time point was significant (P = .16 to .86)

blocks.text: All patients got 1 g IV TXA before incision and in recovery. The EOTXA group added 1.95 g oral TXA daily on POD 1–3. ROM, daily opioid use and assistive-device use did not differ at 2, 6 and 12 weeks (P > .10).

items.message: Adding 3 days of oral TXA on top of standard IV dosing gave no pain, ROM or opioid benefit, so routine extended oral TXA for pain is not supported.
items.why: Largest RCT so far on a protocol some centres adopted after an earlier positive trial, and it was negative.
items.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Examining the Effects of Extended Oral Tranexamic Acid on Postoperative Pain and Range of Motion Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.

items.headline: UKA Survival 85% at 15 Years; Technology and Fixed Bearing Lower Revision Risk

blocks.text: Fixed bearing in 78%; technology assistance in 59% (fluoroscopy 43%, robotic 15%, navigation 1%). 97% of revisions were conversion to TKA. Mean KSS 47 → 75 at 5 years.

items.message: In a large contemporary series UKA was durable, and technology assistance, fixed-bearing design and surgeon volume were each linked to fewer revisions.
items.why: One of the largest single-centre UKA series with 15-year data, and the univariable signals favour the technology-assisted fixed-bearing approach.
items.title: Technology Assistance and Fixed-Bearing Design Were Associated with Higher Revision-Free Survival at 15 Years After UKA: A Cohort Study of 2,234 Consecutive Knees.

items.headline: Gracilis Harvest Stalls Gracilis and Adductor Longus Recovery After ACLR

blocks.label: Interval hypertrophy, 6 → 12 months
blocks.foot: Adductor longus change −2.4 vs +11.1 cm³, P = .020

blocks.text: ST graft used adjustable-button tibial fixation; STG used a tibial screw. No other thigh muscle differed. Gracilis and adductor longus changes were positively correlated.

items.message: Taking the gracilis leaves a persistent muscle deficit that may extend to the adductor longus, which supports semitendinosus-only hamstring grafts.
items.title: Gracilis tendon harvest for ACL reconstruction impairs gracilis muscle volume recovery and may adversely affect adjacent thigh musculature. MRI-based outcomes from a subgroup of patients enroled in the DOSTAR randomized controlled trial.

items.headline: Tibial Cement Pockets Cut Revision for Aseptic Tibial Loosening

blocks.text: Cement pockets present in 4,753 of 8,591 fixed-bearing and 942 of 3,003 mobile-bearing tibial components, across multiple implant designs.

items.message: A recessed cement pocket under the tibial baseplate was associated with fewer revisions for aseptic tibial loosening in fixed-bearing TKA, though all-cause revision was unchanged.
items.title: The presence of cement pockets on the tibial component undersurface is associated with reduced revision for aseptic tibial loosening-A single-centre study of 11,594 total knee arthroplasties.

items.headline: Slope-Reducing Osteotomy With ACLR: 1.7% Graft Failure Regardless of Level or Staging

blocks.text: Certainty of evidence was very low for every outcome. The authors stress this reflects insufficient power, not proven equivalence.

items.message: Anterior closing-wedge HTO with ACLR has a low complication profile whatever the level or staging, but the data cannot yet say whether slope correction itself helps.
items.title: No significant differences in complication and graft failure rates by type of surgery or osteotomy level after slope-reducing osteotomy with ACL reconstruction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

items.headline: LET Doubles the Odds of Early Stiffness After Pediatric ACLR

blocks.metric: Restricted ROM at 3 months (flexion loss ≥15° or extension loss ≥5°)

blocks.text: LET aOR 2 (95% CI 1.01–3.95), female aOR 4.23 (2.09–8.55). Age, PT start, graft type, meniscal surgery, deprivation, insurance and delay to surgery were not associated. MUA or lysis in 8 patients, more often after LET.

items.message: In children LET adds a real but mostly mild and self-limiting stiffness risk, so watch early motion closely, especially in girls.
items.why: LET is spreading fast in pediatric ACLR and this is a 412-knee look at its main downside.
items.title: The Impact of Lateral Extra-Articular Tenodesis on Knee Range of Motion After Pediatric Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.

items.design: Retrospective subset of a phase 3 trial
items.headline: Cord Blood MSC-Hyaluronate Implant Outlasts Microfracture at 5 Years

blocks.metric: Durable repair on MRI (MOCART > 60 at 3 and 5 years, < 10-point change)

blocks.text: KL grade I–III knees. MCID achievement was numerically higher with the implant (50–56% vs 28–31%) but not significant. MOCART scores themselves did not differ, and limb alignment was not associated with outcome.

items.message: Allogeneic cord-blood MSC composite implantation held up better than microfracture at 5 years, clinically and on MRI, in a small retained subset.
items.title: More Durable Cartilage Repair and Better Clinical Outcomes at 5 Years Using Allogeneic Umbilical Cord Blood-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Hyaluronate Composite Implantation Versus Microfracture for Knee Osteoarthritis.

items.headline: Longer Tourniquet Time Means More Opioids, Slower PT and More MUA

blocks.text: Tourniquet groups by inflation time divided by operative time: partial 2,914, until closure 10,003, full 3,690. KOOS JR at 6 weeks did not differ across strategies.

items.message: Keeping the tourniquet up through closure or the whole case was associated with more inpatient opioids, slower mobilisation and more MUA, while a short partial tourniquet carried none of those penalties.
items.why: Very large dataset and the dose-response pattern gives a practical target: inflate for less than 60% of the case.
items.title: The Impact of Tourniquet Duration on Postoperative Opioid Use and Recovery After Total Knee Arthroplasty.

items.headline: Trochlear Bone Marrow Lesions Predict Residual Symptoms After OWHTO

blocks.l: KOOS Symptoms points at 2 years per 1-point trochlear BML grade (95% CI −13.48 to −0.88, P = .03)

items.l: absolute correlation coefficients, WORMS BML vs KOOS

blocks.text: Lysholm, every KOOS subscale and alignment improved significantly at 2 years. Model adjusted for age, BMI and 2-year HKA angle. Trochlear BML lowered the absolute score, not the gain.

items.message: A trochlear bone marrow lesion on the preoperative MRI flags patients who will keep more symptoms after OWHTO even though they still improve.
items.title: Evaluation of Prognostic Factors in Medial Open-Wedge High Tibial Osteotomy Using Preoperative Semiquantitative MRI Findings.

items.design: Modified Delphi consensus (22 international experts, 3 rounds)
items.headline: Expert Consensus: Centralize When Root-Tear Extrusion Exceeds 3 mm

rows: Medial root repair, extrusion > 3 mm on MRI
Lateral root tear + meniscofemoral ligament injury + extrusion > 3 mm
Transtibial, anchor or hybrid all acceptable; avoid overtightening

blocks.text: Aims cited: reduce extrusion, improve contact mechanics, possibly aid root healing and limit repair displacement. Also applies to meniscal allograft transplantation. Long-term joint-protective benefit still unproven.

items.message: The panel endorsed centralization as an adjunct to root repair and transplantation when extrusion exceeds 3 mm, with no single fixation method preferred.
items.why: First international consensus on a technique that originated in Japan and is now spreading, with a concrete 3 mm threshold.
items.title: Indications, Techniques, and Outcomes of Meniscus Centralization for Root Tears and Meniscus Transplantation: An International Expert Consensus Statement.

items.headline: Oxinium Onlay PFA: 81% Survival at 10 Years, 75% at 20

blocks.text: 41 revisions in total, most often for OA progression (24). Sex, age and side had no effect on survival.

items.message: A modern onlay PFA loses about a quarter of implants by 20 years, mainly to OA progression, so patient selection remains the key.
items.title: Clinical outcome of a modern patellofemoral arthroplasty prosthesis into the second decade - a cohort study with minimum 10-year follow-up.

glossary.def: Surgery that replaces a torn anterior cruciate ligament with a tendon graft placed in bone tunnels or sockets.
A muscle on the inner thigh that pulls the leg toward the midline. It lies next to the gracilis.
A way of fixing a ligament graft in which a small button sits on the outer bone surface and a loop of suture can be tightened to pull the graft into the tunnel.
Statistical correction for other factors, such as age or sex, that could distort the link between a treatment and an outcome. Unadjusted results ignore these factors.
An arthroscopic method done entirely through the joint without open incisions or full bone tunnels, used for meniscal repair, root repair or ACL reconstruction with short sockets.
Coming from another person of the same species, such as donor cells or donor tissue.
An osteotomy in which a wedge of bone is removed from the front of the upper tibia to flatten a steep tibial slope, lowering strain on the ACL or its graft.
The ligament in the centre of the knee that stops the tibia sliding forward and controls rotation. It is often torn in pivoting sports.
The Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute system for bone loss in revision knee replacement: type 1 (minor), 2A and 2B (damaged bone in one or both condyles), and 3 (major loss).
A measure from a ROC curve of how well a test or score separates two groups. 0.5 means no better than chance and 1.0 means perfect.
Loss of fixation of an implant to the bone without infection. It is a leading reason for revision of joint replacements.
Repeat surgery on a joint replacement done for causes other than infection, such as loosening, instability or wear.
Coming from the patient's own body, such as cells or tissue taken from and returned to the same person.
Replacing two compartments of the knee with separate partial implants while keeping the cruciate ligaments and the healthy compartment.
Arthritis affecting two of the knee's three compartments, often the inner and the patellofemoral ones.
Keeping patients, doctors or assessors unaware of which treatment was given, to reduce bias. In a double-blind study, neither patients nor those treating or assessing them know.
Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared, used as a rough measure of body fat.
Bone marrow drawn from the patient, often from the pelvis, and spun down to concentrate cells and growth factors for use in healing tissue.
An area of abnormal signal in the bone under the cartilage on MRI, thought to reflect swelling, micro-damage or overload. It is linked to pain and progression of osteoarthritis.
An ACL graft taken from the middle third of the patient's own patellar tendon, with a bone block at each end for strong bone-to-bone healing.
A technique that repairs a torn ACL by placing a protein scaffold soaked in the patient's blood between the torn ends, so the ligament can heal instead of being replaced.
A description of outcomes in a group of patients who all had the same treatment, with no comparison group. It cannot show that a treatment is better than another.

A study that compares patients who had an outcome with similar patients who did not, to find factors linked to that outcome. In surgical journals the label is often used for any retrospective comparison.
A recessed area on the underside of a tibial tray that fills with bone cement, giving the cement more grip on the implant.
A technique that anchors the outer edge of an extruded meniscus back to the edge of the tibia to reduce extrusion and restore load-sharing.
A rating, from very low to high, of how much confidence can be placed in a pooled result, based on study design, bias, consistency and precision.
Protecting joint cartilage from damage or breakdown.
An observational study that follows groups of people over time and compares outcomes between those with and without an exposure or treatment.
A scan that uses X-rays from many angles to build cross-sectional and 3D images. It shows bone shape and rotation in detail.
A range of values that likely contains the true effect. A 95% CI that crosses the 'no effect' value (0 for differences, 1 for ratios) means the result is not statistically significant.

How much a knee implant's design limits movement to give stability, ranging from cruciate-retaining to posterior-stabilised, varus-valgus constrained and hinged. More constraint puts more stress on fixation.
An experiment done in a laboratory, for example on animals or cadavers, under controlled conditions with a comparison group.
Total knee replacement done after an earlier knee operation such as an osteotomy or partial knee replacement.

glossary.term: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee
glossary.def: A system that sorts knees into nine phenotypes using two angles from the femur and tibia: the overall limb alignment and the direction the joint line slopes. Used to plan personalised knee replacement alignment.
A knee replacement design that keeps the patient's posterior cruciate ligament instead of removing it.
A blood clot in a deep vein, usually of the leg, which can happen after joint replacement. Part of it can travel to the lungs.
A way of reaching expert agreement by asking a panel to rate statements in several rounds, showing them the group's answers between rounds, until agreement is reached.
A pattern in which an effect grows step by step as the amount of exposure grows. Finding it makes a causal link more believable.
Correcting leg alignment by cutting both the lower femur and the upper tibia, so large deformities can be corrected while keeping the joint line closer to horizontal.
Abnormal blood sugar levels, covering both prediabetes and diabetes.
A knee replacement design in which the plastic insert is locked to the tibial tray and does not move on it.
A 12-item questionnaire asking how often patients are aware of their artificial or treated joint in daily life. Scored 0 to 100; higher is better, meaning the joint is more 'forgotten'.
A class of drugs, such as semaglutide, that copy a gut hormone to lower blood sugar and reduce appetite. Used for diabetes and obesity.
A blood test showing average blood sugar over about the past three months. Used to diagnose and monitor diabetes and prediabetes.
A thin muscle on the inner thigh that helps bend the knee and pull the leg inward. Its tendon is often taken together with the semitendinosus for ligament grafts.
The gradual change of an ACL graft into ligament-like tissue, often judged by MRI signal; lower signal suggests a more mature graft.
A comparison of how fast an event, such as failure, happens over time in one group compared with another. A value above 1 means the event happens sooner or more often.
Cutting and realigning the upper tibia to shift weight from a worn inner compartment to the healthier outer one. In open-wedge HTO, a gap is opened on the inner side.
Plastic bearing material treated with radiation to link its molecules more tightly, making it wear less than the conventional type.
A highly constrained knee replacement in which the femoral and tibial parts are linked by a hinge. Used for severe instability or bone loss, mostly in revisions.
The angle between the mechanical axes of the femur and tibia on a standing long-leg radiograph. It describes overall varus or valgus alignment of the limb.
A natural molecule in joint fluid and cartilage that gives it its slippery, cushioning quality. It is used as a joint injection and as a carrier for cells.
A graft that combines the patient's tendon with a synthetic tape or other material, intended to add early strength.
A factor that remains linked to an outcome after the analysis accounts for other factors.
A meniscal repair in which sutures are passed from inside the joint out through the capsule and tied over it through a small incision.

glossary.term: International Knee Documentation Committee subjective knee form
glossary.def: A widely used patient questionnaire on knee symptoms, sports activity and function, common after ligament and meniscus surgery. Scored 0 to 100; higher is better.
The range covering the middle half of the values, from the 25th to the 75th percentile. Often shown with a median when data are skewed.
Given directly into a vein.
Muscle strength measured on a machine that moves the joint at a constant speed, giving torque through the range of motion.
Muscle strength measured while the muscle contracts without the joint moving, for example pushing against a fixed bar at a set knee angle.
The gap between the bones on an X-ray, which mostly reflects cartilage and meniscus thickness. Narrowing suggests arthritis.
How much the knee joint line tilts from horizontal on standing images. Too much tilt after osteotomy may increase shear forces on cartilage.
A grading of knee arthritis on plain X-ray from 0 (none) to 4 (severe), based on bone spurs, joint space narrowing, sclerosis and bone deformity. Higher means more severe.
A knee replacement alignment method that aims to restore the patient's own pre-arthritic joint lines and limb alignment, rather than a neutral straight limb.
An excessive, irrational fear of movement and physical activity because of expected pain or re-injury. It can slow recovery after injury or surgery.

glossary.term: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score
glossary.def: A patient questionnaire with five subscales: pain, other symptoms, daily living, sport and recreation, and knee-related quality of life (QoL). Each subscale is scored 0 to 100; higher is better.
A knee replacement rating with a knee part (pain, motion, stability, alignment) and a function part (walking, stairs). Newer versions add patient-reported sections. Higher is better.
A short 7-item version of KOOS for knee replacement and arthritis, covering stiffness, pain and daily function. Converted to a 0 to 100 score; higher is better.
Also called the Anterior Knee Pain Scale; a 13-item questionnaire for patellofemoral pain and patellar instability. Scored 0 to 100; higher is better.
The angle on the outer side between the femoral mechanical axis and the joint surface of the lower femur, normally about 88 degrees. Higher values mean varus at the femur.
A procedure added to ACL reconstruction on the outer side of the knee, such as anterolateral ligament reconstruction or lateral tenodesis, to better control rotational instability.
A procedure added to ACL reconstruction in which a strip of the iliotibial band is passed under the lateral collateral ligament and fixed to the femur, to add control of rotation.
A crack through the intact outer bone bridge (the hinge) during or after open-wedge high tibial osteotomy. It can make the correction unstable.
Platelet-rich plasma prepared to remove most white blood cells, which is thought to cause less inflammation. Often preferred for injections into joints.
The injured leg's result divided by the uninjured leg's, as a percentage, for strength or hop tests. Often used to guide return to sport, typically aiming for at least 90%.
Reduced knee bending or straightening after injury or surgery, often from scar tissue (arthrofibrosis). It may need manipulation or surgery to release.
An 8-item patient questionnaire on knee symptoms such as instability, locking, pain and swelling, often used after ligament surgery. Scored 0 to 100; higher is better.
Cutting or releasing scar tissue inside a joint, usually arthroscopically, to restore motion.
A scan using a strong magnet and radio waves to show soft tissues such as cartilage, menisci, ligaments and bone marrow, without radiation.

glossary.term: Magnetic Resonance Observation of Cartilage Repair Tissue
glossary.def: An MRI score that rates the quality of cartilage repair tissue, such as filling of the defect and integration with the surrounding cartilage, from 0 to 100. Higher is better.
Forcibly bending a stiff joint while the patient is anaesthetised, to break scar tissue and regain motion, usually after knee replacement or ligament surgery.
An RSA measure of implant migration: the largest 3D movement of any point on the implant. Early high values can predict later loosening.
The traditional knee replacement method that places components at right angles to the bone axes to make a straight, neutral limb.
The ligament on the inner side of the knee that resists valgus (knock-knee) force.
How far the inner joint space opens under a valgus force, often compared with the other knee, to measure medial collateral ligament laxity.
A tear at or near the back attachment of the inner meniscus to the tibia. It causes loss of hoop function, extrusion and fast cartilage wear if untreated.
The main soft-tissue restraint that stops the patella moving outward, running from the inner femur to the patella. It is usually torn in patellar dislocation.
Surgery that rebuilds the main inner soft-tissue restraint of the patella with a graft to stop it from dislocating.
The angle on the inner side between the tibial mechanical axis and the joint surface of the upper tibia, normally about 87 degrees. Lower values mean varus at the tibia.
Replacing a missing or badly damaged meniscus with a donor meniscus, usually in younger patients after meniscectomy.
Outward displacement of the meniscus beyond the edge of the tibia, usually measured on MRI or ultrasound. It shows lost hoop function, often after a root tear.
One of the ligaments running from the back of the lateral meniscus to the medial femoral condyle. They help hold the lateral meniscus in place.
A tear of the meniscus at or near its attachment to the tibia. It lets the meniscus slip out of the joint and loads the cartilage as if the meniscus were gone.
Cells, also called mesenchymal stromal cells, that can develop into bone, cartilage or fat cells and release healing signals. Studied as a treatment to aid tissue repair.
A statistical method that combines the results of several similar studies into one overall estimate, giving more precision than any single study.
A cartilage repair technique in which small holes are made in the exposed bone so that marrow cells can form a scar-like repair tissue.
The smallest change in a score that patients notice as meaningful. Used to judge whether a statistically significant result matters in practice.
A statistical model for repeated measurements on the same people over time. It handles the link between a person's own measurements and copes with some missing visits.
A knee replacement design in which the plastic insert can rotate or slide on the tibial tray, intended to lower wear and better match natural motion.
A unit that converts doses of different opioid drugs into the equivalent dose of morphine, so that total opioid use can be compared.
An increase in the size of a muscle, usually from training or recovery after injury.
A heart attack: death of heart muscle caused by blocked blood flow in a coronary artery.
The United Kingdom's national database of joint replacement operations, used to track implant survival and revisions.
The American College of Surgeons database of surgical patients with standard data on 30-day complications, readmissions and reoperations.
Electrical current applied through skin pads to make muscles contract. Used after knee surgery to reduce quadriceps weakness and inhibition.
Failure of a fracture or osteotomy to heal. Delayed union means healing is slower than expected but still progressing.
Normal blood sugar levels.
A result whose difference could easily be due to chance, usually meaning the P value was above 0.05.
A grading system from the Osteoarthritis Research Society International for how much cartilage damage is seen under the microscope, used in human and animal studies. Higher means worse damage.
A comparison of the odds of an outcome in one group with those in another. A value above 1 means higher odds, below 1 lower odds.
A trochlear implant that sits on top of the cut front surface of the femur, as opposed to an inlay implant set into the bone.
Substances from the body, such as platelets, cells or growth factors, used to try to improve healing of bone, cartilage, tendon or ligament.
Degenerative joint disease with loss of cartilage, bone changes and pain. It is the most common reason for knee replacement.
A grading of cartilage damage seen at arthroscopy or on MRI, from grade 0 (normal) to grade 4 (full-thickness loss with exposed bone). Higher is worse.
A 12-item patient questionnaire on knee pain and function, mainly used after knee replacement. Scored 0 to 48; higher is better.
A metal alloy whose surface is heated to form a thin ceramic layer, used for implant bearing surfaces to lower wear and friction.
A condition in which the patella slips partly or fully out of its groove, usually outward. Often recurs after a first dislocation.
The angle of the patella relative to the femoral condyles or trochlea on axial imaging. Excess tilt suggests patellar maltracking.
A partial knee replacement that resurfaces only the trochlea of the femur and the back of the patella, for arthritis limited to that joint.
The score threshold on an outcome measure beyond which most patients consider their current condition acceptable. It describes a satisfactory state, not an amount of change.
A questionnaire filled in by the patient about their own symptoms, function or quality of life, rather than measured by a doctor.
A large randomized trial that tests a new treatment against a standard or placebo to confirm benefit and safety, usually the last step before approval.
Supervised exercise, movement and manual treatment used to restore strength, motion and function after injury or surgery.
Making many small needle punctures in a tight ligament, often the MCL, to lengthen it slightly. Used to widen a tight medial joint for access or to balance a knee.

A clinical test of rotational knee instability after ACL injury, in which the partly dislocated tibia suddenly slips back into place as the knee bends under valgus and internal rotation. Graded 0 (none) to 3 (gross).
A concentrate of platelets made from the patient's own blood and injected to try to aid healing or reduce symptoms, as in knee arthritis.
Prepared or done at the bedside or in the clinic during the same visit, instead of being sent to a laboratory.
The plastic used for the bearing surface of joint replacements. Its wear particles can cause bone loss and implant loosening.
The backward tilt of the upper tibial joint surface seen from the side. More slope pushes the tibia forward and can increase load on the ACL.
A count of days after an operation, with the day of surgery as day 0. Used to time measurements and events.
Blood sugar that is higher than normal but not high enough for diabetes. It raises the risk of later diabetes.
A method for observational studies that pairs treated and untreated patients with a similar likelihood of receiving the treatment, based on their characteristics, so the groups are more comparable.
A study planned in advance in which data are collected as patients are followed forward in time.
Blockage of a lung artery, usually by a blood clot from a leg vein. It can be life-threatening.
An ACL or other ligament graft taken from the patient's own quadriceps tendon, either soft tissue only or with a bone block from the patella.
A precise X-ray method that uses small metal beads and paired images to measure tiny movements of implants or wear over time, often to predict loosening.
A study in which participants are assigned to treatments by chance, so the groups are alike except for the treatment. It is the strongest single design for testing whether a treatment works.
How far a joint can bend and straighten, measured in degrees. For the knee it is usually reported as the extension deficit and the maximum flexion.
Another repeat operation on a joint replacement that has already been redone at least once.
A large, ongoing database that records every procedure of a certain type, such as joint replacements, in a region or country. Used to track results and trends.
The share of patients who reach a predefined level of improvement, such as a set drop in pain. It turns a continuous score into a yes-or-no result for each patient.
A version of the patient-specific alignment method that copies the patient's native alignment only within set safe limits, and corrects it if it falls outside them.
A study that looks back at data already recorded, such as medical records. It is quicker but more open to bias than a study planned in advance.
Going back to a sport after injury or surgery. Studies may separate returning at all from returning to the pre-injury level.
Surgery to replace some or all parts of a previous knee replacement, for reasons such as loosening, instability, infection or wear.
Also called relative risk; the risk of an outcome in one group divided by the risk in another. A value below 1 means the outcome is less common in the first group.
Knee replacement in which a robotic system helps plan and carry out bone cuts and implant position, aiming for higher precision.
Surgery that reattaches a torn meniscal root to the tibia to restore the meniscus's load-sharing hoop function.
A French research group based in Lyon that publishes large cohort studies on ACL reconstruction, especially with lateral extra-articular procedures.
A new analysis of data already collected for another study, often asking a question the original trial was not designed to answer. Results suggest ideas rather than prove them.
A hamstring tendon on the inner back of the thigh. It is the main tendon taken for hamstring grafts in ligament reconstruction.
A ligament graft made from both the semitendinosus and the gracilis tendons, folded to make a thicker graft.
A measure of how widely values are spread around their mean. A small value means the results cluster closely.
A difference between group means divided by the spread of the data, so studies using different scales can be combined. About 0.2 is small, 0.5 moderate and 0.8 large.

The mix of cells left after fat tissue is broken down and the fat cells removed. It contains stem and stromal cells, blood vessel cells and immune cells, and is injected into joints as a biologic treatment.

glossary.term: Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the knee
glossary.def: A stress fracture in the bone just under the cartilage, usually of the medial femoral condyle, from normal loads on weakened bone. Often linked to meniscal root tears.
An analysis done in only part of a study population, such as one treatment arm or one age group. Results are less reliable than the main analysis.
The proportion of implants or repairs still in place, without failure or further surgery, at a given time after the operation.
A curved hooked instrument used arthroscopically to pass sutures through tissue, for example in posterior horn meniscal repairs through a posteromedial portal.
A review that searches for all studies on a clear question using set, reproducible methods, then appraises and summarises them.
A questionnaire measuring fear of movement and of re-injury. The 11-item version is scored 11 to 44; higher means more fear.

A single rating of a person's work and sports activity level, from 0 (sick leave or disability) to 10 (competitive pivoting sport at national or elite level). Higher means a more demanding activity level.
Cutting and moving the bony bump where the patellar tendon attaches, then fixing it with screws, to improve patellar tracking or unload patellar cartilage.
Hip replacement surgery in which both the ball and socket are replaced with implants.
Knee replacement surgery in which the joint surfaces of the femur and tibia, and often the patella, are replaced with metal and plastic implants.
A cuff inflated around the thigh to stop blood flow and keep the operative field clear of blood during knee surgery.
A drug that slows the breakdown of blood clots and so reduces bleeding during and after surgery. It is given by vein, by mouth or into the joint.
A meniscal root fixation in which sutures through the torn root are pulled down a tunnel drilled in the tibia and tied over the front of the tibia.
A global research network that pools anonymised electronic health records from many healthcare organisations, used for large observational studies.
Enlargement of the bone tunnels after ACL reconstruction, seen on X-ray or CT. It matters mainly because it can complicate revision surgery.

glossary.term: Umbilical cord blood-derived mesenchymal stem cell
glossary.def: Stem cells taken from donated umbilical cord blood and grown in culture. They can be mixed with hyaluronic acid and implanted into a cartilage defect.
Partial knee replacement in which only one worn compartment, usually the inner one, is replaced.
Abnormal opening of the inner side of the knee under an outward-bending force, usually from medial collateral ligament injury or release.
A group term for deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
A line on which patients mark how strong a feeling is, most often pain, usually scored 0 to 10 or 0 to 100. For pain, higher means worse pain.
Measuring the volume of a structure such as a muscle by outlining it on each slice of an MRI or CT scan.

glossary.term: Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index
glossary.def: A patient questionnaire for hip and knee arthritis with pain, stiffness and physical function sections. Higher scores mean worse symptoms, unless the score has been reversed.
A detailed MRI scoring system for knee osteoarthritis that grades features such as cartilage, bone marrow lesions, osteophytes and menisci in each region of the joint. Higher means more damage.
